title: BadWAM: When World-Action Models Dream Right but Act Wrong
abstract: arXiv:2607.15207v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: World-action models (WAMs) are emerging as a promising foundation for embodied control: rather than predicting actions alone, they learn representations that couple action generation with future world prediction. This coupling is often viewed as a source of robustness, interpretability, and safety, as a robot's action can in principle be checked against its imagined future. In this paper, we show that this assumption is fragile. We introduce BadWAM, a unified framework for modeling and evaluating World-Action Drift Attacks: a new class of WAM-specific adversarial attacks that use small visual perturbations to break the alignment between what a WAM imagines and what it executes. BadWAM characterizes this attack surface along two natural criteria: attack strength and stealthiness. When the adversary prioritizes disruption, BadWAM instantiates an action-only adversarial attack, which directly drives the model toward task-failing actions

translated_title: BadWAM：当世界-动作模型想象正确但行动错误时
translated_abstract: 世界-动作模型正成为具身控制领域一种有前景的基础：它们不再仅仅预测动作，而是学习将动作生成与未来世界预测耦合在一起的表示。这种耦合通常被视为鲁棒性、可解释性和安全性的来源，因为机器人的动作原则上可以根据其想象的未来进行检验。在本文中，我们证明这一假设是脆弱的。我们提出了BadWAM，一个用于建模和评估“世界-动作漂移攻击”的统一框架：这是一类专门针对WAM的新型对抗性攻击，利用微小的视觉扰动来破坏WAM所想象的内容与其实际执行内容之间的对齐。BadWAM从两个自然的标准来刻画这一攻击面：攻击强度和隐蔽性。当攻击者优先考虑破坏效果时，BadWAM实例化了一种仅针对动作的对抗性攻击，直接驱使模型产生导致任务失败的动作。
tldr: 本文提出BadWAM统一框架，揭示了世界-动作模型中动作与预测的耦合并非安全保证——微小的视觉扰动即可破坏模型想象与执行之间的对齐，使其“想象正确但行动错误”。
en_tdlr: BadWAM introduces a unified framework for World-Action Drift Attacks, demonstrating that small visual perturbations can break the alignment between what world-action models imagine and what they actually execute, undermining their assumed safety and robustness.
